content:
Apple's annual September event is fast approaching, with the company set to unveil three new iPhone models: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here's a roundup of all the rumours.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will succeed the popular 17 Pro series as the new flagship lineup.

Rumoured features include:

  • A20 Pro chip, delivering a step up in performance and efficiency
  • Major camera upgrades, with a variable aperture on the main camera being a particularly exciting highlight
  • 35% smaller Dynamic Island for a sleeker, more modern design
  • A new colour option headlined by a bold wine red
  • The best battery life ever, with the iPhone 18 Pro Max seeing especially significant gains
  • Redesigned Camera Control button
  • Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem
  • New satellite connectivity features, including 5G satellite links

The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to see a price hike. Market estimates suggest a starting price of around US$1,399, though the writer reckons the actual figure will be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is rumoured to be Apple's first-ever foldable phone, with a price tag expected to exceed US$2,000, creating an entirely new premium tier.

The foldable design makes the iPhone Ultra the most groundbreaking model in Apple's history. The device will adopt a wide book-style fold, with an outer display of around 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches — essentially an iPad mini.

The build quality is expected to match that of the iPhone Air, with a titanium frame and a sleek silhouette.

The iPhone Ultra will feature two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide) plus two front-facing cameras serving the inner and outer displays respectively. Biometric authentication will use Touch ID rather than Face ID.

Software will be the biggest highlight of the device, with iOS 27 supporting split-screen multitasking and adaptive landscape display layouts perfectly suited to the new foldable form factor.

Performance is expected to be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, featuring the same A20 Pro chip, a vapour chamber cooling system, and the C2 modem.

Missing models: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

Normally, we'd expect the September event to bring not just the flagships but also the new iPhone 18 base model and the successor to the iPhone Air.

However, reports suggest Apple will significantly shake up its autumn lineup this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It's unclear whether this is a strategic move or simply a forced response to the current memory supply crunch. Either way, with the more affordable models absent, this autumn's iPhone lineup will be entirely focused on the high end.

Are you planning to upgrade your iPhone this autumn? Which model has caught your eye? Let us know in the comments.
